name: Hyaluronic acid
lead: Hyaluronic acid is a glycosaminoglycan found in skin and joints, used in topical serums for hydration and in cross-linked injectable gels as dermal fillers. Topical products temporarily plump and hydrate the surface, while fillers add structural volume to lips, cheeks and folds.

Claims that it holds roughly a thousand times its weight in water refer to laboratory behavior; in practice topical benefits are mostly short-term hydration, whereas injectables have stronger clinical evidence for volume restoration.

paras: As a humectant polymer, it binds large amounts of water in the skin surface or in injected gel. Cross-linked fillers physically add volume and may stimulate modest collagen production through tissue stretch.

Topical forms are very well tolerated. Injectable fillers can cause bruising, swelling and lumps, and rare vascular occlusion leading to tissue necrosis or vision loss, which makes provider skill critical. Fillers are medical devices requiring trained injectors.
